title: Pricing the Overadvance Portion of an Operating Lines of Credit Advance
content:
The overadvance fee on the Operating Lines of Credit is priced on the line's latest advance; every earlier advance was priced, or found within its available credit, on the day it was drawn.

## Definitions

- **Outstanding principal before the advance**: the line's principal worked out from its transaction history — advances plus returned principal payments less principal payments — less the advance itself.
- **Lending limit**: the lower of the commitment and the borrowing base on the line's most recent certificate when the product requires a borrowing base, and the commitment when it does not.
- **Available credit immediately before the advance**: on a revolving product, the lending limit less the outstanding principal before the advance; on a product that is not revolving, which runs a single term, the commitment less every earlier advance booked on the line.
- **Overadvance portion**: the advance amount less the available credit immediately before it, and never less than zero.
- **Fee**: the overadvance portion multiplied by the product's overadvance fee rate, read as a percentage, rounded once to cents.

## Worked figure (hypothetical Borrowing Base Operating Line, overadvance fee rate 1.00%)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Commitment | USD 2,000,000.00 |
| Borrowing base on the most recent certificate | USD 1,500,000.00 |
| Lending limit — the lower of the two | USD 1,500,000.00 |
| All advances on the line, the latest of USD 320,123.45 included | USD 1,720,123.45 |
| Principal payments; returned principal payments | USD 150,000.00; none |
| Principal from the transaction history | USD 1,570,123.45 |
| Outstanding principal before the advance | USD 1,570,123.45 less USD 320,123.45, that is USD 1,250,000.00 |
| Available credit immediately before the advance | USD 1,500,000.00 less USD 1,250,000.00, that is USD 250,000.00 |
| Overadvance portion | USD 320,123.45 less USD 250,000.00, that is USD 70,123.45 |
| Fee | USD 70,123.45 multiplied by 1.00%, that is USD 701.2345, rounded once to USD 701.23 |

Had the latest advance been USD 240,000.00 with the same history before it, the available credit of USD 250,000.00 would have covered it, the overadvance portion would be zero, and the fee would be zero.
